All these protective effects of GMET o were largely abolished by co-treatment with dorsomorphin, ccumulation and inflammation to preserve normal hepatocyte multi-targeting compound to improve steatohepatitis. eatohepatitis · AMPK · Lipid accumulation · Inflammation Introduction The prevalence of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) in Asia has increased from 25 to 34% since early 2000, which is as high as that in Europe and North America (Yip et al. Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH), a more advanced inflammatory stage of NAFLD, develops in up to 25% of all cases (Zhou et al. NASH is closely associated with multiple metabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), dyslipidemia, and other metabolic co-morbidities (Younossi et al. Moreover, NASH notably contributes to liver-related deaths as it ultimately progresses to liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, which is the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide (Chalasani et al. 2018; Lu et al. The impending public health burden imposed by NASH has provoked drastic interest in the disease from clinicians, the pharmaceutical industry, and scientists.

However, until now, weight loss through the implementation of healthy lifestyle modifications (diet and physical exercise), which are difficult to sustain, is still recognized as the most effective and 2‑Geranyl‑1‑methoxyerythrabyssin II alleviates lipid accumulation and inflam cost-efficient method to rectify not only NASH but also other co-morbidities of metabolic syndromes (Zhou et al. Furthermore, liver transplantation is a reliable therapy for NASH treatment, but the shortage of donors has led to a growing focus on novel pharmacotherapies to address the urgent need for treating NASH (Wong et al. AMP-activated kinase (AMPK), a central regulator of lipid metabolism and inflammation, is a potential target for NASH treatment (von et al. Activated AMPK negatively regulates the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) (Inoki et al. 20, which further regulates several target proteins involved in lipid metabolism, such as sterol regulatory element-binding proteins-1c (SREBP1c) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) (Shimano 2000; Düvel et al. AMPK also mediates lipogenesis by regulating acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) (Day et al. On the other hand, inflammatory cytokines, such as tumor necrosis factors (TNFs) and interleukins (ILs), stimulate the swift transcription of genes, mainly via the activation of the nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) pathway (Lu et al. Activated AMPK alleviates the inflammatory response via inhibition of NF-κB (Kracht et al. Conversely, during lipid metabolism, activated protein kinase B (AKT) induces mTOR activation, which leads to lipid accumulation through the activation of multiple proteins, such as SREBP1 and ACC (Yecies et al. 2011; Yuan et al. Previous studies have reported that the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway plays a crucial role in pro-inflammatory gene expression during inflammation by activating the IκBkinase (IKK)/NF-κB pathway (Lu et al. Pterocarpans are the second largest group of isoflavonoids.

They contain a tetracyclic ring system derived from the flavonoid skeleton and have two chiral centers at the carbon atoms C-6a and C-11a (Selvam et al. Certain pterocarpans exhibit numerous bioactivities, including antioxidant, antimalarial, anticancer, and antimicrobial effects (Selvam et al. 2017; Tarbeeva et al. 20, while some pterocarpans possess remarkable anti-obesity and anti-inflammatory properties; for example, maackiain significantly reduces adipogenesis in human adipocytes and decreases inflammation in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice (Guo et al. 2021; Mladenova et al. Furthermore, supplementation with pterocarpans can reduce the risk factors associated with diabetes and dyslipidemia in patients with obesity and mild metabolic syndrome, while also simultaneously decreasing inflammatory-related gene expression in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (Ryu et al. As part of our ongoing research investigating natural bioactive products for treating NAFLD, we observed that a methanol (MeOH) extract from Lespedeza bicolor roots exhibited markedly hepatoprotective effects on oleic acid (OA)-treated primary mouse hepatocytes.

Bioassay-guided fractionation and chemical investigation of L. bicolor roots resulted in the isolation of a new mmation in… 809 pterocarpan, 2-geranyl-1-methoxyerythrabyssin II (GMET), which had not been described previously.
In this study, OA-treated primary mouse hepatocytes were used to mimic the influx of excess free fatty acids into hepatocytes, giving rise to steatohepatitis.
We investigated the hepatoprotective effects of GMET and the underlying signaling pathways.
Additionally, methionine-cholinedeficient (MCD) diet-induced NASH mice were used to further demonstrate the effects of GMET.
This study provides a novel potential multi-targeting compound to improve steatohepatitis.

Isolation and identification of a new pterocarpan, 2‑geranyl‑1‑methoxyerythrabyssin II Bioassay-guided fractionation led us to isolate GMET, a major component of Lespedeza bicolor.
To isolate GMET, compounds from the roots of dried L. bicolor (1.7 kg) were extracted using 100% methanol with ultrasonication at room temperature.
The methanolic extract (203.2 g) from which the solvent was removed in a vacuum was dissolved in H O and fractionated with ethyl acetate (51.1 g) and n-hexane (6.0 g).

The 8 10 ethyl acetate fraction was subjected to silica gel column chromatography and eluted with a CH Cl -MeOH solvent mixture (100:1 to 1:100, v/v), which yielded five fractions (E1–E. Each fraction (E1–E was evaluated for its preliminary lipid-lowering effect by measuring the triglyceride (TG) contents in OA-induced primary hepatocytes.

Subfraction E1 (16.4 g), which showed the best effect among E1 to E5, was separated using semipreparative high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with 75% CH CN in H O to yield five subfractions (M1–M. Subsequently, the five subfractions (M1–M were screened further for the lipid-lowering effect and M5 was selected for further fractionation.

The separation of subfractions from M5 (1.5 g) yielded GMET (79.5 mg) (purity > 98%, HPLC analysis) using HPLC with 85% CH CN in H O. We named this compound 2-geranyl-1-methoxyerythrabyssin II (GMET) since the only difference with 1-methoxyerythrabyssin II was the geranyl group at C-2 (Thuy et al. Isolation and culture of primary hepatocytes Primary hepatocytes were isolated and cultured from the livers of 6 to 8-week-old C57BL/6 J male mice, according to the methods used in previous studies (Hu et al. After the cell concentration and viability were measured, the hepatocytes were seeded in collagen-coated dishes and grown in 5% CO at 37 °C in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (Thermo Fisher) and 1% penicillin–streptomycin (Solarbio, Beijing, China).
Oleic acid‑induced steatohepatitis and its inhibition by GMET Hepatocytes were treated with 1 mM OA-conjugated 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) for 24 h to induce steatohepatitis.
The extent of intracellular lipid accumulation was determined by Oil red O (ORO) staining and TG content assays.

The OA-induced hepatocytes were pretreated with different concentrations of GMET dissolved in DMSO (Solarbio) for 30 min. In parallel, hepatocytes were treated with 1% OA-free BSA and an equal volume of DMSO as the normal control.
Animal treatment Eight-week-old male C57BL/6 J mice were purchased from Vital River Laboratories (Beijing, China).
All mice were maintained under specific pathogen-free, standard light conditions (12 h light/dark cycle) at room temperature (22–24 °C).
The mice were randomly divided into four groups after 7 days of adaptive feeding.
The normal control group consumed an untreated MCD diet (Trophy Feed Technology, Jiangsu, China).
In the other three groups, the mice were fed an MCD diet before treatment with 10 mg/ kg or 20 mg/kg GMET via intragastric gavage every day for 4 weeks.
Dorsomorphin (10 mg/kg) was administered by gavage every 2 days for 6 weeks.
MCD feeding lasted for 5 weeks.
Mice treated with the vehicle (blank solution) served as controls and were subjected to the same experimental approaches in parallel with those in the control and untreated groups.
All animal protocols were approved by the Animal Care and Use Committee of Wenzhou Medical University.
At the end of the experiment, animals were injected intraperitoneally with pentobarbital sodium (1% v/v) for anesthesia.
Peripheral blood was collected and centrifuged to obtain serum for biochemical analyses and cytokine measurements.

Liver tissues were rapidly removed and stored at -80 °C for further use. Western blotting analysis Cells were seeded at a density of 1 × 105 cells/mL in 25 c m2 flasks, and the hepatocytes were pretreated with or without 5 μM dorsomorphin (MCE, Shanghai, China) for 2 h and with different concentrations of GMET for 30 min before induction with OA for 24 h. The cells were then harvested and lysed with radioimmunoprecipitation assay (RIPA) lysis buffer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) containing 1 × protease and phosphatase inhibitor cocktails (Roche Molecular Biochemicals, Basel, Switzerland).

Next, the protein concentrations of the cellular lysates were measured using a bicinchoninic acid protein assay kit (Beyotime, Haimen, China), and equal amounts of the proteins were separated using sodium dodecyl sulfate–polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (10–12%; Beyotime).

AMPK and AKT are involved in the GMET‑induced reduction of lipid accumulation in OA‑treated hepatocytes Based on the above results, we evaluated the impact of GMET on the AKT/mTOR pathway, as it is the major inducer of de novo lipogenesis. 3A–C, GMET induced a dramatic reduction in AKT phosphorylation at Ser473.
Additionally, the phosphorylated form of mTOR (Ser24 was lowered at the protein level, as evidenced by immunoblotting.
Fully activated AKT regulates multiple metabolic processes, including de novo lipogenesis, through mTOR-dependent pathways in response to free fatty acid accumulation.
On the other hand, these results also established the possible involvement of mTOR in AMPK-mediated lipid amelioration in GMET-treated steatosis hepatocytes.
As a major sensor of cellular energy status, AMPK also directly affects lipid metabolism by phosphorylating and inactivating acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC).

The phosphorylation levels of AMPK and ACC were determined to explore the molecular mechanism of GMET in the treatment of hepatic steatosis in vitro (Fig. OA induced the downregulation of AMPK (Thr1 phosphorylation, whereas GMET treatment markedly increased the ratio of p-AMPK (Thr1/AMPK and p-ACC (Ser/ACC, which enhanced the inhibition of lipid accumulation.
We know that mTOR is a key regulator of lipid metabolism and an immediate upstream mediator of SREBP1 and PPARα expression.

The expression of hepatic lipid metabolism-related proteins and genes were measured to further confirm the potential role of GMET in lipid metabolism (Fig. OA treatment decreased the mRNA expression of Pparα and Hsl, which are involved in fatty acid β-oxidation and lipolysis, whereas GMET treatment increased the expression of these genes together with the protein level of PPARα.

In contrast, the OA group showed remarkably upregulated Srebp1 expression, together with its target genes Acc, Fas, and Scd1; however, GMET treatment remarkably downregulated SREBP1 protein levels, leading to a decrease in the expression of its target genes.

GMET alleviates inflammation and blocks the nucleus translocation of p65 in OA‑treated primary hepatocytes We also evaluated the impact of GMET on inflammation, which is pivotal for the triggering and progression of NASH.
As shown in Figs. 4A and B, GMET reduced the gene expression and protein levels of TNFα and IL-6, together with the mRNA levels of iNos and Il-1β, which were induced by OA stimulation in hepatocytes.
It is well known that NF-κB is a critical, central factor in the stimulation of inflammation.
NF-κB-p65 plays an essential role as a transcription factor of the NF-κB family and is an important component of the IκBα and p65/ p50 complex in the cytosol.
Therefore, we determined the preventive effect of GMET on the OA-induced expression of the proteins associated with NF-κB activation.
The results indicate that GMET weakened the OA-induced phosphorylation of IKK, IκBα, and p65 (Fig. Furthermore, we extracted nuclear p65 to determine the changes in p65 nuclear translocation.

OA induced the nuclear localization of p65, which was then blocked by GMET treatment; this finding was supported by the immunofluorescence results (Fig. Dorsomorphin attenuates the effects of GMET in OA‑treated primary hepatocytes Lastly, we investigated whether AMPK plays a key role in the GMET mediation of both lipid metabolism and inflammation.
Dorsomorphin (an AMPK inhibitor) reversed the GMET-induced decrease in the intracellular lipid and TG content.

Meanwhile, the levels of TNFα released into the supernatant were increased by dorsomorphin treatment (Fig. 5E–H, dorsomorphin blocked the effects of mTOR, ACC, SREBP1, PPARα, and p65, but not AKT or IKK, which were induced by GMET.
These findings indicate that GMET partially alleviated lipid accumulation and inflammation by activating AMPK.
